It was established to implement the National AIDS Control Programme (NACP) to prevent and control the spread of HIV/AIDS in India. Key functions include: 1) Screening high-risk groups for HIV, 2) Conducting public education campaigns to promote safe sex practices, 3) Providing free antiretroviral therapy (ART) to HIV-positive individuals, and 4) Ensuring blood safety through screening of blood donations. While NACO may indirectly support orphans affected by HIV/AIDS, facilitating adoption is not its primary mandate.
fields.mnemonic: NACO's 3 main tasks: 'Screen, Educate, Treat' (SET). Remember: 'NACO SETs the standard for HIV control in India.'

fields.question_text:
Prophylactic oophorectomy is recommended in high risk women with which of the following?
1. Carrying BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes
2. Family history of breast, colon, ovarian cancer
3. Patients having tubo-ovarian abscess

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Prophylactic oophorectomy is recommended in high-risk women with BRCA1 or BRCA2 gene mutations and those with a family history of breast, colon, or ovarian cancer due to elevated lifetime risk of ovarian cancer. Tubo-ovarian abscess is not an indication for prophylactic oophorectomy.
fields.concept_explanation: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumor suppressor genes associated with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome. Women carrying mutations in these genes have a significantly increased lifetime risk of ovarian cancer (up to 40-60% for BRCA1 and 15-20% for BRCA2). Prophylactic oophorectomy reduces this risk by approximately 80-90%. A family history of related cancers also elevates risk, warranting consideration of risk-reducing surgery. Tubo-ovarian abscess is an infectious condition, not a hereditary cancer risk factor.
fields.mnemonic: BRCA = Breast/Ovarian Cancer Risk Always; Family history = Follow High-risk Assessment

fields.question_text: 'Schiller-Duval body' is a characteristic histological feature of which one of the following cancers?
fields.explanation: Schiller-Duval bodies are pathognomonic histological features of endodermal sinus tumors (yolk sac tumors), characterized by glomeruloid structures resembling primitive glomeruli.
fields.concept_explanation: Endodermal sinus tumors (ESTs) are rare malignant germ cell tumors of the ovary, derived from yolk sac elements. Schiller-Duval bodies are diagnostic hallmarks, consisting of a central blood vessel surrounded by tumor cells within a cystic space, mimicking the endodermal sinus of the rat placenta. These tumors secrete alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), aiding in diagnosis and monitoring.
fields.mnemonic: Think 'Yolk Sac' = 'Y' for 'Schiller-Duval' bodies. Alternatively, 'S-D' for 'Sinusoid-like Duval' structures.

fields.question_text: Which one of the following is the distinguishing feature to differentiate Gartner's cyst from Cystocele?
fields.option_a: Marked cough impulse in Gartner's cyst
fields.option_b: Margins are ill-defined in Gartner's cyst
fields.option_c: There is no impulse on coughing in cystocele
fields.explanation: Gartner's cyst is a remnant of the Wolffian duct and does not communicate with the bladder, hence no cough impulse. Cystocele, being a herniation of the bladder into the vagina, may show a cough impulse due to bladder descent.
fields.concept_explanation: Gartner's cyst is a benign vaginal cyst derived from remnants of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, typically located along the lateral vaginal wall. It is usually asymptomatic and does not communicate with the bladder or urethra. Cystocele, on the other hand, is a type of pelvic organ prolapse where the bladder descends into the vaginal canal, often due to weakening of the pelvic floor muscles. During a Valsalva maneuver (e.g., coughing), the descent of the bladder in cystocele can be palpable or visible, whereas Gartner's cyst remains stationary as it is not connected to the bladder.
fields.mnemonic: Gartner's cyst = 'G' for 'Gone' (no cough impulse), Cystocele = 'C' for 'Cough' (impulse present).

fields.question_text: Surgical treatment by 'ventrosuspension of uterus' is used for what condition?
fields.explanation: Ventrosuspension of the uterus is a surgical procedure used to correct retroversion of the uterus by suspending it to the anterior abdominal wall, thereby relieving symptoms associated with this positional abnormality.
fields.concept_explanation: Retroversion of the uterus refers to a condition where the uterus is tilted backward instead of its normal forward tilt (anteversion). While often asymptomatic, retroversion can cause symptoms like dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, or infertility in some cases. Ventrosuspension (e.g., Gilliam or Baldy-Webster procedures) involves suspending the uterus to the anterior abdominal wall or round ligaments to correct the retroverted position. This procedure is distinct from treatments for prolapse (options A and D) or uterine rupture (option C).
fields.mnemonic: Think 'Ventrosuspension = Ventro (front) + Suspension (lifting up)'. It corrects the uterus tilted backward (retro) by lifting it forward (ventro).

fields.question_text: A 29-year-old female with 3 months amenorrhoea presents to gynaecology OPD with complaints of something coming out of her vagina. On clinical evaluation she was found to have single live pregnancy with second degree uterine prolapse. Which one of the following is the best management plan for her?
fields.explanation: The patient has a live pregnancy with second-degree uterine prolapse. Cerclage operation is the best management to prevent preterm delivery due to cervical incompetence associated with prolapse.
fields.concept_explanation: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) during pregnancy is rare but can lead to complications like preterm labor or miscarriage. Uterine prolapse in pregnancy is managed conservatively unless there is cervical incompetence or risk of preterm delivery. Cerclage (cervical stitch) is performed to reinforce the cervix and prevent preterm birth. Cervical amputation is not indicated in pregnancy. Pessary is contraindicated in pregnancy due to risk of infection and pressure effects. Reassurance is insufficient as the prolapse may worsen and threaten the pregnancy.
fields.mnemonic: CERCLAGE: Cervical support, Ensures, Reduces, Labour risk, Cervical incompetence, Live pregnancy, Avoids preterm, Gestational safety, Ensures term delivery

fields.question_text:
During delivery of HIV infected women, which of the following are recommended?
Zidovudine (ZDV) is given at the onset of labour.

Elective caesarean delivery reduces the risk of vertical transmission.

Amniotomy and oxytocin augmentation should be done.

Antiretroviral therapy should be given to all neonates.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Zidovudine (ZDV) is given at the onset of labour, elective caesarean delivery reduces vertical transmission risk, and antiretroviral therapy should be given to all neonates born to HIV-infected mothers. Amniotomy and oxytocin augmentation are not recommended as they may increase transmission risk.
fields.concept_explanation: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) of HIV involves interventions during pregnancy, labour, and postpartum to reduce the risk of vertical transmission. Zidovudine (ZDV) is an antiretroviral drug administered during labour to the mother. Elective caesarean delivery (before labour or rupture of membranes) is recommended to reduce transmission risk, especially in women with high viral loads. Neonatal antiretroviral therapy (ART) is given to all exposed infants to further reduce transmission risk. Procedures like amniotomy (artificial rupture of membranes) and oxytocin augmentation are avoided as they may increase the risk of transmission by exposing the infant to maternal blood and fluids.
fields.mnemonic: Z-CAN: Zidovudine during labour, Caesarean delivery, Avoid amniotomy/oxytocin, Neonatal ART.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following can be a complication in the baby due to post maturity of pregnancy?
1. Meconium aspiration
2. Hypoglycemia
3. Intra ventricular haemorrhage
4. Polycythemia

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Post-mature babies (born after 42 weeks) are at risk of meconium aspiration, hypoglycemia, and polycythemia due to placental insufficiency and reduced nutrient supply. Intraventricular hemorrhage is more common in preterm infants, not post-term.
fields.concept_explanation: Post-term pregnancy (gestation >42 weeks) leads to placental aging, reduced oxygen and nutrient supply to the fetus. This causes fetal stress, leading to meconium passage (risk of aspiration), hypoglycemia (due to depleted glycogen stores), and polycythemia (compensatory erythropoiesis from chronic hypoxia). Intraventricular hemorrhage is primarily a complication of prematurity due to fragile cerebral vasculature.
fields.mnemonic: POST-MATURE: P (Placental insufficiency), O (Oxygen deprivation), S (Stress → Meconium), T (Thin placenta → Hypoglycemia), M (Meconium aspiration), U (Uteroplacental insufficiency → Polycythemia), R (Reduced reserves), E (Exclude IVH as preterm complication).

fields.question_text:
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy presents with which of the following features?
Pruritus after 28 weeks gestation, especially in palms and soles

Serum bilirubin levels > 5 mg%

Raised levels of serum bile acids

Features subside within two weeks postpartum

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is characterized by pruritus (especially on palms and soles) after 28 weeks gestation, elevated serum bile acids, and resolution within 2 weeks postpartum. Serum bilirubin levels >5 mg% are not a typical feature.
fields.concept_explanation: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is a liver disorder unique to pregnancy, caused by impaired bile flow due to hormonal changes (e.g., estrogen and progesterone). It leads to accumulation of bile acids in the liver and bloodstream, causing pruritus (itching) without rash. Pruritus typically starts in the third trimester (after 28 weeks) and resolves within 2 weeks postpartum. Serum bile acids are the most sensitive marker, while bilirubin elevation is usually mild (<5 mg%).
fields.mnemonic: P-B-R: Pruritus (palms/soles), Bile acids (raised), Resolves postpartum (2 weeks).

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are blood values of Iron Deficiency Anaemia?
Serum iron is less than 30 µgm/100 mL

Total iron binding capacity is less than 400 µgm/dL

Percentage saturation is 10% or less

Serum ferritin is below 30 µgm/L

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Serum iron <30 µgm/100 mL, percentage saturation ≤10%, and serum ferritin <30 µgm/L are diagnostic of Iron Deficiency Anaemia. TIBC is elevated (>400 µgm/dL), not reduced.
fields.concept_explanation: Iron Deficiency Anaemia (IDA) results from inadequate iron for hemoglobin synthesis. Serum iron falls due to depleted stores, TIBC rises as transferrin production increases to bind available iron, saturation drops as iron is scarce, and ferritin (iron storage protein) declines reflecting depleted iron reserves.
fields.mnemonic: SAT-Fer: Serum iron low, TIBC high, saturation low, Ferritin low → IDA.

fields.question_text:
Clinical features of an infant with Fetal growth retardation at birth include which of the following?
1. Physical features give 'an old man look'.
2. Baby is alert, reflexes are normal.
3. There is presence of weight deficit.
4. Thick fat accumulates around shoulders of baby.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Fetal growth retardation (FGR) at birth presents with physical features resembling an old man ('old man look'), normal alertness and reflexes, and a weight deficit. Thick fat accumulation around shoulders is not a typical feature of FGR.
fields.concept_explanation: Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) refers to a fetus that has not reached its growth potential due to various maternal, placental, or fetal factors. Infants with FGR often exhibit a characteristic 'old man look' due to reduced subcutaneous fat, wrinkled skin, and a disproportionate head-to-body ratio. They may appear alert and have normal reflexes despite their small size. Weight deficit is a hallmark of FGR, but excessive fat accumulation, especially around the shoulders, is not typical. This condition is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality.
fields.mnemonic: FGR: 'OLD MAN' - O: Old man look (wrinkled skin), L: Low birth weight, D: Disproportionate head, M: Alert and normal reflexes, A: Absence of excessive fat (e.g., around shoulders), N: Normal alertness.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are correct regarding 'Chhaya' contraceptive?
It has potent anti-estrogenic and weak estrogenic property.

Failure rate is 1–4 per HWY (Hundred Women Years) of use.

It inhibits ovulation.

It creates asynchrony between zygote and endometrium.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Chhaya is a non-steroidal contraceptive with potent anti-estrogenic and weak estrogenic properties. It has a low failure rate of 1–4 per HWY and creates asynchrony between zygote and endometrium by altering endometrial receptivity. It does not inhibit ovulation.
fields.concept_explanation: Chhaya is a non-hormonal contraceptive developed in India, primarily acting as an anti-estrogen with weak estrogenic effects. It alters the endometrial environment to prevent implantation rather than inhibiting ovulation. Its failure rate is comparable to other reversible contraceptives like IUCDs. The asynchrony between zygote and endometrium is due to its effect on endometrial maturation, making it unreceptive to implantation.
fields.mnemonic: CHHAYA: C - Creates asynchrony, H - High anti-estrogen, H - Has weak estrogen, A - Alters endometrium, Y - Yields low failure rate (1-4/HWY).

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are examples of LARC (Long Acting Reversible Contraceptives)?
1. Copper-T 380A
2. Implants
3. LNG-IUS

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: All three options (Copper-T 380A, Implants, and LNG-IUS) are recognized as Long Acting Reversible Contraceptives (LARCs).
fields.concept_explanation: Long Acting Reversible Contraceptives (LARCs) are highly effective, long-term birth control methods that are reversible upon discontinuation. They include intrauterine devices (IUDs) like Copper-T 380A and hormonal IUDs like LNG-IUS (Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system), as well as contraceptive implants. These methods are preferred for their efficacy, safety, and convenience, with durations of action ranging from 3 to 10 years depending on the type.
fields.mnemonic: LARCs = LARge, Long-term, Reversible Contraceptives. Think: 'LARCs are LARge (effective), Long-lasting, and Reversible when you want to conceive.'

fields.question_text: How many times in a year does withdrawal bleeding occur in extended continuous regimens of combined oral contraceptive pills?
fields.explanation: In extended continuous regimens of combined oral contraceptive pills, withdrawal bleeding typically occurs 4 times a year (once every 3 months).
fields.concept_explanation: Extended continuous regimens of combined oral contraceptive pills involve taking active pills continuously for an extended period (e.g., 3 months) followed by a short hormone-free interval (usually 4-7 days) to induce withdrawal bleeding. This regimen reduces the number of withdrawal bleeds per year compared to the traditional 21/7 cycle (13 times a year). The 3-month cycle (4 times a year) is a common extended regimen to minimize menstrual bleeding while maintaining contraceptive efficacy.
fields.mnemonic: Think '4 seasons in a year' for 4 withdrawal bleeds in extended regimens. Traditional cycles have 13 bleeds (52 weeks/4 weeks), but extended regimens space them out to 4 times a year.

fields.question_text: Bilateral total salpingectomy is recommended surgical procedure to reduce the risk of:
fields.explanation: Bilateral total salpingectomy reduces the risk of epithelial ovarian cancer by removing the fallopian tubes, which are a primary site for precursor lesions (e.g., serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma) linked to ovarian cancer.
fields.concept_explanation: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most lethal gynecological malignancy. Recent evidence suggests that many high-grade serous ovarian cancers originate from the fallopian tube epithelium, particularly in the fimbrial end. Bilateral salpingectomy removes these precursor sites, thereby reducing the risk of ovarian cancer. This procedure is now recommended as a risk-reducing strategy, especially in women undergoing other pelvic surgeries (e.g., hysterectomy) or those with BRCA mutations.
fields.mnemonic: SALPINGECTOMY = 'Saves Against Ovarian Cancer, Prevents Invasive Growth, Not Just Endometriosis, Greatly Extends Years' (SALPINGECTOMY).

fields.question_text: Tongue bite occurs in eclampsia at:
fields.explanation: Tongue bite occurs during the tonic phase of eclamptic seizures due to sustained muscle contraction.
fields.concept_explanation: Eclampsia is characterized by generalized tonic-clonic seizures in a patient with preeclampsia. The tonic phase involves sustained muscle contraction, leading to rigidity and potential tongue biting. The clonic phase follows with rhythmic jerking movements. Coma and postictal stages occur after the seizure activity.
fields.mnemonic: Tonic Tongue: Tonic phase = Tongue bite. Remember 'T' for both.

fields.question_text:
Indication for removal of IUDs include which of the following?
1. Perforation of uterus
2. Pregnancy with device in situ
3. One year after menopause
4. Persistent migraine

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Indications for IUD removal include uterine perforation, pregnancy with the device in situ, and one year after menopause. Persistent migraine is not a standard indication for IUD removal.
fields.concept_explanation: Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) are long-acting reversible contraceptives. Removal is indicated in cases of complications such as perforation (where the IUD may migrate outside the uterine cavity), pregnancy with an IUD in place (to reduce risks like miscarriage or preterm labor), and after menopause (as the device is no longer needed once hormonal cycles cease). Persistent migraine is not a recognized indication for IUD removal unless it is directly linked to the device, which is rare.
fields.mnemonic: P.U.M.P. - Perforation, Unwanted Pregnancy, Menopause, Persistent issues (only P, U, M are valid for removal).

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are the absolute contraindications for the use of combined oral contraceptive pills?
1. Severe hypertension
2. Pregnancy
3. Diabetes with retinopathy
4. Gall bladder disease

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Absolute contraindications for combined oral contraceptive pills include severe hypertension, pregnancy, and gall bladder disease. Diabetes with retinopathy is a relative contraindication.
fields.concept_explanation: Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCs) contain estrogen and progestin, which can increase the risk of complications in certain conditions. Severe hypertension, pregnancy, and gall bladder disease are absolute contraindications due to the risk of thromboembolism, fetal harm, and exacerbation of gall bladder issues, respectively. Diabetes with retinopathy is a relative contraindication because COCs may worsen vascular complications.
fields.mnemonic: Pregnancy, Hypertension, Gall bladder disease: 'PHG' (Pregnancy, Hypertension, Gall bladder) are absolute no-nos for COCs.

fields.question_text: A 27-year-old recently married female comes to family planning clinic requesting for long term reversible contraception. Which one of the following is the best suited option for her?
fields.explanation: Nexplanon (progestin-only implant) is the best long-term reversible contraception for a 27-year-old female due to its high efficacy (>99%), reversibility, and suitability for recent marriage without estrogen-related risks.
fields.concept_explanation: Long-term reversible contraception options include progestin-only methods (e.g., Nexplanon, hormonal IUDs) and combined hormonal methods (e.g., COCs). Nexplanon is a subdermal implant releasing etonogestrel for 3 years, ideal for patients seeking high efficacy without estrogen (e.g., smokers, breastfeeding, or those with contraindications to estrogen). Diaphragms are user-dependent and less effective; Chhaya is a copper IUD (not reversible in the short term). Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) are reversible but not long-term (typically taken daily).
fields.mnemonic: LARCs for LARCs: Long-Acting Reversible Contraceptives (IUDs, implants) are best for long-term reversible needs. Nexplanon = 'N' for 'No estrogen, No daily pill, No user error' (high efficacy).

fields.question_text: Which one of the following is an indication for cold knife conisation?
fields.option_a: Treatment of Nabothian follicle on ectocervix
fields.option_b: Inconsistent findings of colposcopy, cytology and directed biopsy
fields.option_d: Squamous cell carcinoma cervix stage IIA
fields.explanation: Cold knife conisation is indicated when there is inconsistency between colposcopy findings, cytology results, and directed biopsy results, requiring a diagnostic and therapeutic excision.
fields.concept_explanation: Cold knife conisation (CKC) is a surgical procedure used to remove a cone-shaped piece of tissue from the cervix. It is primarily indicated for diagnostic purposes when there is a discrepancy between colposcopic findings, cytology (Pap smear), and biopsy results. This inconsistency may suggest a need for a larger tissue sample to rule out or confirm precancerous or cancerous changes. CKC is also used therapeutically for treating high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) or early-stage cervical cancer.
fields.mnemonic: DISCREPANCY = Cold knife conisation. D (Discrepancy in findings), I (Inconsistent colposcopy, cytology, biopsy), S (Suspicious for high-grade lesion), C (Cold knife conisation), R (Removal of tissue for diagnosis/therapy), E (Excision of abnormal tissue), P (Pathology evaluation), A (Assess for malignancy), N (Next steps based on results), C (Confirmatory treatment if needed), Y (Yes, it's indicated).

fields.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding female sterilization?
It can be done 24–48 hours following delivery.

Ideal time for interval ligation is luteal phase preceding menstruation.

It can be combined with medical termination of pregnancy.

It is a preventive measure against serous ovarian cancer.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct. Female sterilization can be performed 24–48 hours post-delivery (postpartum sterilization), can be combined with medical termination of pregnancy (MTP), and is a preventive measure against serous ovarian cancer. Statement 2 is incorrect as the ideal time for interval ligation is not the luteal phase but typically during the follicular phase or any time unrelated to menstruation.
fields.concept_explanation: Female sterilization is a permanent contraceptive method involving surgical procedures like tubal ligation or non-surgical methods like Essure (now largely obsolete). Postpartum sterilization is safe and effective within 24–48 hours of delivery due to the accessibility of the fallopian tubes. Interval sterilization is usually performed during the follicular phase to avoid the luteal phase, which may coincide with pregnancy. Sterilization can be combined with MTP if both procedures are medically indicated. Epidemiological studies suggest that tubal ligation reduces the risk of serous ovarian cancer, possibly due to reduced ovarian exposure to carcinogens or inflammation.
fields.mnemonic: P-P-S-C: Postpartum sterilization is safe; Pair with MTP if needed; Serous ovarian cancer risk is reduced; Avoid luteal phase for interval ligation.

fields.question_text: The most popular technique of tubal ligation is:
fields.explanation: The Pomeroy technique is the most commonly used method for tubal ligation due to its simplicity, effectiveness, and low complication rate.
fields.concept_explanation: Tubal ligation is a permanent method of female sterilization where the fallopian tubes are occluded to prevent the ovum from reaching the uterus. The Pomeroy technique involves creating a loop in the midportion of the fallopian tube, ligating it with absorbable sutures, and excising the loop. This method is preferred for its ease of performance, reliability, and reversibility potential compared to other techniques like Madlener (crushing and tying without excision) or Uchida (dissection and reanastomosis). Cornual resection involves removing the cornual portion of the tube near the uterus, which is less common due to higher complication risks.
fields.mnemonic: Pomeroy = Popular, Practical, Preferred for tubal ligation. Think 'PPP' for Pomeroy, Popular, Preferred.

fields.question_text: Which one of the following is defined as "the average number of children a woman would have if she were to pass through her reproductive years, bearing children at the same rates as the women now in each age group"?
fields.explanation: Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is the average number of children a woman would have over her reproductive lifespan, assuming she experiences the same age-specific fertility rates as the current population.
fields.concept_explanation: Fertility rates are demographic measures used to assess reproductive health. TFR is a key indicator that summarizes fertility levels by estimating the average number of children per woman. It is calculated by summing age-specific fertility rates across all reproductive ages (typically 15-49 years). Unlike ASFR (fertility rate for a specific age group) or GFR (fertility rate per 1,000 women aged 15-44), TFR provides a comprehensive view of fertility trends. NRR adjusts TFR for mortality, indicating the average number of daughters a woman would have who survive to reproductive age.
fields.mnemonic: TFR = 'Total Fertility Rate' = 'Total' children a woman would have over her 'entire Fertility period'.

fields.question_text:
Which among the following is correct about yellow fever vaccination requirement for international travellers?
Term of validity of the certificate is changed from 10 years to the duration of the life of the vaccinated person, some years ago.

Lifetime validity of the certificate applies automatically to all existing and new certificates.

Validity of the certificate begins 4 days after vaccination.

In India, booster dose of yellow fever vaccine is required for those whose certificate is prior to the year 2016. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Options 1 and 2 are correct: The validity of the yellow fever vaccination certificate was changed from 10 years to lifetime validity, and this applies to all existing and new certificates. Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Validity begins immediately after vaccination (not 4 days later), and no booster dose is required in India for certificates issued before 2016.
fields.concept_explanation: Yellow fever vaccination requirements are governed by the International Health Regulations (IHR). The World Health Organization (WHO) updated the validity of the yellow fever vaccination certificate in 2016, changing it from a 10-year validity to lifetime validity. This change applies retroactively to all existing certificates and new ones issued after the update. The certificate is valid from the date of vaccination, and no booster doses are required. Countries may have specific requirements, but India does not mandate a booster dose for yellow fever vaccination certificates issued before 2016.
fields.mnemonic: YF-LIFE: Yellow Fever - Lifetime Immunization Valid Forever Everywhere. Remember: Validity is lifetime, starts immediately, and no boosters needed.

fields.question_text:
Regarding active immunization against Typhoid fever, consider the following statements:
The typhoid polysaccharide vaccine is injectable and can be given subcutaneously or intramuscularly.

The typhoid polysaccharide vaccine is required to be given in two doses and administered on 0 and 7th day.

The typhoid oral Ty21a vaccine requires to be given in three doses on 0, 3rd and 7th days.

Protective immunity with typhoid vaccines is achieved immediately after the vaccine is received.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
fields.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. The injectable typhoid polysaccharide vaccine is given subcutaneously or intramuscularly. Statement 2 is incorrect (no two-dose schedule on 0 and 7th day for polysaccharide vaccine). Statement 3 is incorrect (oral Ty21a vaccine requires three doses on alternate days, not 0, 3rd, and 7th days). Statement 4 is incorrect (immunity is not immediate; it takes time to develop).
fields.concept_explanation: Active immunization against typhoid fever includes two types of vaccines: (1) Injectable Vi polysaccharide vaccine (ViCPS), administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly, typically in a single dose with booster every 2-3 years. (2) Oral Ty21a vaccine, given as three doses on alternate days (e.g., 0, 2, 4 or 0, 3, 7 days), with booster doses every 5 years. Protective immunity develops gradually over weeks, not immediately.
fields.mnemonic: For typhoid vaccines: 'Vi' is injected (ViCPS), 'Ty' is taken (Ty21a). Vi = Inject, Ty = Try (oral). Doses: Vi = 1 shot, Ty = 3 sips.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Mantoux test for tuberculosis?
It entails injecting 1 TU (Tuberculin Unit) of PPD (Purified Protein Derivative) in 0.1 mL intradermally.

The injection should be given with the needle bevel facing downward.

When placed correctly, the injection should produce a pale wheal of the skin, 1–2 mm in diameter.

The injection should be given with a tuberculin syringe.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: Mantoux test uses 1 TU of PPD in 0.1 mL intradermally and requires a tuberculin syringe. Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect: the needle bevel should face upward, and the wheal should be 6–10 mm in diameter.
fields.concept_explanation: The Mantoux test is an intradermal skin test used to diagnose tuberculosis infection. It involves injecting 1 TU (0.1 mL) of PPD intradermally using a tuberculin syringe. The needle bevel should face upward to ensure proper intradermal placement, and the injection should produce a wheal of 6–10 mm in diameter. The test is read 48–72 hours later by measuring the induration (not erythema) at the injection site.
fields.mnemonic: Mantoux: 1 TU, 0.1 mL, Upward bevel, Wheal 6–10 mm, Tuberculin syringe (M-T-U-W-T).

fields.question_text: Which one among the following types of ventilation, best fits the following description – "A system of ventilation in which fresh air is blown into the room by centrifugal fans so as to create a positive pressure, and displace the vitiated air"?
fields.explanation: Plenum ventilation is a system where fresh air is mechanically blown into a room under positive pressure, displacing vitiated (contaminated) air, matching the given description.
fields.concept_explanation: Ventilation systems are categorized based on airflow mechanisms. Plenum ventilation uses centrifugal fans to force fresh air into a space, creating positive pressure that pushes out stale air. This is distinct from exhaust ventilation (which removes air), balanced ventilation (equal supply and exhaust), and natural ventilation (relying on natural air movement). It is commonly used in industrial or healthcare settings to control airborne contaminants.
fields.mnemonic: Plenum = Positive Pressure; think 'P' for Push (fresh air in) and 'P' for Positive pressure.

fields.question_text: The 'Nalgonda Technique' developed by the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) was developed primarily for the removal of which one of the following from water?
fields.explanation: The Nalgonda Technique is a defluoridation method developed by NEERI to remove excess fluorine from water, primarily to prevent fluorosis.
fields.concept_explanation: The Nalgonda Technique is a cost-effective, community-level method for defluoridation of water. It involves the addition of alum (aluminum sulfate) and lime to water, followed by rapid mixing, flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration. This process reduces fluoride levels to safe limits (below 1.5 mg/L) by forming insoluble aluminum fluoride complexes. It is particularly useful in areas with high natural fluoride content in groundwater.
fields.mnemonic: Nalgonda = 'No Longer Go N' (No Longer Go Near) high Fluoride water. Think: 'Nalgonda Technique = No Fluoride in water.'

fields.question_text:
Smoking is considered to be a modifiable risk factor for Coronary Heart Disease. Consider the following statements with regard to possible mechanisms on the basis of which it acts as a risk factor:
Nicotine stimulation of adrenergic drive raises the blood pressure and myocardial oxygen demand.

It increases carbon monoxide and induces atherogenesis.

It leads to fall in protective high density lipoproteins.

It reduces the apolipoprotein-B plasma levels.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
fields.explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect because smoking reduces apolipoprotein-A1 (not B), which is protective, and does not lower apolipoprotein-B.
fields.concept_explanation: Smoking contributes to coronary heart disease (CHD) through multiple mechanisms: (1) Nicotine stimulates the sympathetic nervous system, increasing heart rate, blood pressure, and myocardial oxygen demand, which can lead to ischemia. (2) Carbon monoxide from smoking binds to hemoglobin, reducing oxygen-carrying capacity and promoting atherogenesis by damaging endothelial cells and increasing oxidative stress. (3) Smoking lowers protective high-density lipoproteins (HDL), which are involved in reverse cholesterol transport and have anti-inflammatory properties. (4) Apolipoprotein-B (apoB) levels are typically elevated in smokers due to increased very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) production and reduced clearance, not reduced.
fields.mnemonic: SMOKE: S - Sympathetic stimulation (nicotine), M - Monoxide (CO) toxicity, O - Oxidative stress (atherogenesis), K - Kills HDL (lowers protective lipoproteins), E - Elevated apoB (atherogenic lipoproteins).

fields.question_text: The expected outcome of Government of India's initiative 'SUMAN' is:
fields.option_a: Zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths
fields.option_b: Limit preventable maternal and newborn deaths to between 0.5–1%
fields.option_c: Limit preventable maternal and newborn deaths to between 1–2%
fields.option_d: Limit preventable maternal and newborn deaths to between 2–5%
fields.explanation: SUMAN aims for zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths by ensuring quality healthcare access.
fields.concept_explanation: SUMAN (Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan) is a Government of India initiative launched in 2019 under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. It focuses on providing assured, dignified, and respectful care to every woman and newborn during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum period. The goal is to eliminate preventable maternal and newborn deaths through quality healthcare services, zero tolerance for denial of services, and respectful maternity care.
fields.mnemonic: SUMAN: 'S'afe 'U'terus 'M'other 'A'nd 'N'ewborn – Zero preventable deaths.

fields.question_text: Water contamination with high content of which chemical can lead to methaemoglobinaemia?
fields.explanation: High nitrate content in water can oxidize hemoglobin to methaemoglobin, reducing oxygen-carrying capacity and leading to methaemoglobinaemia.
fields.concept_explanation: Methaemoglobinaemia is a condition where iron in hemoglobin is oxidized from Fe2+ (ferrous) to Fe3+ (ferric) state, forming methaemoglobin. This form cannot bind oxygen, causing cyanosis and hypoxia. Nitrates (NO3-) in water are reduced to nitrites (NO2-) in the body, which then oxidize hemoglobin to methaemoglobin. Infants are particularly susceptible due to lower levels of methaemoglobin reductase enzyme.
fields.mnemonic: NITRATES → NITRITES → OXIDIZE → METHAEMOGLOBIN → CYANOSIS (N-N-O-M-C)

fields.question_text:
With reference to human body's requirement for proteins, they are essential because they are:
a key supply source for energy.

required for maintenance of osmotic pressure within the intravascular compartment.

critical for upkeep of cell mediated immune response.

vital for the synthesis of certain hormones.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
fields.explanation: Proteins are essential for maintaining osmotic pressure (statement 2), cell-mediated immune response (statement 3), and synthesis of certain hormones (statement 4). Statement 1 is incorrect as proteins are not a primary energy source; carbohydrates and fats serve that role.
fields.concept_explanation: Proteins play multifaceted roles in human physiology. They are crucial for maintaining colloidal osmotic pressure in the intravascular compartment by contributing to plasma oncotic pressure, which prevents fluid leakage into tissues. Proteins are also vital for cell-mediated immunity, as they form antibodies, cytokines, and other immune molecules. Additionally, many hormones (e.g., insulin, growth hormone) are protein-based or derived from amino acids. While proteins can provide energy (4 kcal/g), they are not the body's primary energy source, which is typically derived from carbohydrates and fats.
fields.mnemonic: P.R.O.T.E.I.N.S: P = Pressure (osmotic), R = Repair (tissues), O = Osmotic balance, T = Transport (e.g., hemoglobin), E = Enzymes, I = Immunity, N = Nutrition (growth), S = Synthesis (hormones).

fields.question_text: Which food proteins among the following are considered to be the best and are used in nutritional studies as 'reference protein'?
fields.explanation: Egg proteins are considered the 'reference protein' due to their high biological value and complete amino acid profile, making them ideal for nutritional studies.
fields.concept_explanation: A reference protein is a standard against which other proteins are compared to assess their nutritional quality. It must contain all essential amino acids in proportions that closely match human requirements. Egg proteins (ovalbumin, ovotransferrin, etc.) have a Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS) of 1.0, the highest possible, indicating they provide all essential amino acids in optimal ratios. This makes them the gold standard for evaluating protein quality in diets and nutritional research.
fields.mnemonic: Eggs are the 'E'xcellence standard for protein quality (E for Egg, E for Excellence).

fields.question_text:
Consider the following statements with reference to 'trans fatty acids':
They are geometrical isomers of cis-unsaturated fatty acids.

Though atherogenic, being unsaturated they are less so than saturated fatty acids.

It takes years for trans fatty acids to be flushed from the body.

They lower both LDL cholesterol and HDL cholesterol in the body.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
fields.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Trans fatty acids are indeed geometrical isomers of cis-unsaturated fatty acids (1). They are flushed from the body over years due to their stability and incorporation into cell membranes (3). Statement 2 is incorrect as trans fats are more atherogenic than saturated fats. Statement 4 is incorrect as trans fats raise LDL and lower HDL cholesterol.
fields.concept_explanation: Trans fatty acids (TFAs) are unsaturated fats with at least one double bond in the trans configuration, unlike cis fats which are more common in nature. TFAs are primarily artificial, formed during hydrogenation of vegetable oils. They are more atherogenic than saturated fats due to their adverse effects on lipid profiles: increasing LDL (bad cholesterol) and decreasing HDL (good cholesterol). TFAs are incorporated into cell membranes, making their elimination from the body slow (years). Their consumption is linked to increased risk of coronary heart disease, diabetes, and inflammation.
fields.mnemonic: TRANS fats: T - Trans (bad), R - Raise LDL, A - Atherogenic, N - Not natural (mostly artificial), S - Slow to leave body.

fields.question_text:
Consider the following disorders:
1. Delayed motor milestones
2. Extrapyramidal spasticity
3. Nyctalopia
4. Hearing defects

Which of the above disorders occur as part of the spectrum of iodine deficiency disorders?
fields.explanation: Delayed motor milestones, extrapyramidal spasticity, and nyctalopia are part of the spectrum of iodine deficiency disorders. Hearing defects are not typically associated with iodine deficiency.
fields.concept_explanation: Iodine deficiency leads to hypothyroidism, which can cause developmental delays (delayed motor milestones), neurological manifestations like extrapyramidal spasticity due to thyroid hormone's role in brain development, and nyctalopia (night blindness) due to impaired vitamin A metabolism secondary to hypothyroidism. Hearing defects are more commonly linked to other conditions like congenital rubella or genetic disorders.
fields.mnemonic: IODINE DEFICIENCY: Delayed milestones, Extrapyramidal spasticity, Nyctalopia (DEN). Hearing defects are Not included (HIN).

fields.question_text:
With reference to occupational cancers, consider the following statements:
Skin cancer is a common occupational hazard in workers employed in nickel and chromium work.

Cancer bladder is an occupational hazard in workers employed in dye-stuffs and dyeing industry.

Leukaemia can occur on long exposure to benzol.

Lung cancer is typically found in workers employed in electric cable industries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
fields.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Bladder cancer is linked to dye-stuffs/dyeing industry, and leukemia is associated with long-term benzene (benzol) exposure. Statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.
fields.concept_explanation: Occupational cancers arise from exposure to carcinogens in workplace environments. Skin cancer is linked to arsenic, chromium, and nickel (not directly stated in the question). Bladder cancer is strongly associated with aromatic amines in dyes. Leukemia is caused by benzene exposure. Lung cancer is linked to asbestos, chromium, nickel, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, not typically electric cable industries.
fields.mnemonic: Benzene -> Blood cancer (Leukemia), Dyes -> Bladder cancer, Nickel/Chromium -> Skin/Lung cancer.

fields.question_text: If, on amniocentesis, the alpha fetoprotein is found to be elevated in the amniotic fluid, which defect/disorder is the foetus likely to harbour?
fields.explanation: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in amniotic fluid is strongly associated with neural tube defects (e.g., spina bifida, anencephaly) due to leakage of AFP from the fetal cerebrospinal fluid into the amniotic fluid.
fields.concept_explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a fetal protein produced primarily by the yolk sac and fetal liver. During normal pregnancy, AFP crosses the placental barrier into the maternal bloodstream, where it can be measured in maternal serum (MS-AFP) for screening. In cases of neural tube defects (NTDs), the fetal spinal cord or brain is exposed, allowing AFP to leak into the amniotic fluid. This elevated AFP in amniotic fluid (amniocentesis) is a diagnostic marker for NTDs. Other conditions like omphalocele or gastroschisis can also elevate AFP, but NTDs are the most common association. AFP is not typically elevated in cardiac defects, muscular dystrophy, or metabolic disorders like galactosemia.
fields.mnemonic: AFP = 'A Fetal Protein' leaks in 'A Fetal Problem' (Neural tube defects). Remember: High AFP in amniotic fluid = 'Head or spine' issue.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are domains (or types) of learning?
1. Affective learning
2. Cognitive learning
3. Physiological learning
4. Psychomotor learning

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: The three primary domains of learning are Affective (emotional/attitude), Cognitive (knowledge/understanding), and Psychomotor (physical skills). Physiological learning is not a recognized domain.
fields.concept_explanation: Learning domains categorize educational goals into distinct types. Benjamin Bloom's taxonomy classifies learning into three main domains: Affective (feelings/values), Cognitive (mental skills/knowledge), and Psychomotor (physical skills). These domains are foundational in medical education for designing curricula and assessing competencies.
fields.mnemonic: A.C.P. - Affective (Attitude), Cognitive (Knowledge), Psychomotor (Physical skills). Remember 'ACP' like the medical acronym for Acute Coronary Syndrome.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are beneficiaries of services provided under the Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS)?
1. Adolescent boys
2. Adolescent girls
3. Pregnant women
4. Children less than 6 years of age

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: ICDS beneficiaries include adolescent girls, pregnant women, and children under 6 years. Adolescent boys are not covered under ICDS.
fields.concept_explanation: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme is a government program in India launched in 1975 to combat malnutrition, illiteracy, and poverty. It provides food, preschool education, primary healthcare, immunization, health check-ups, and nutrition education to vulnerable groups: children aged 0-6 years, pregnant and lactating women, and adolescent girls (11-18 years). Adolescent boys are excluded from this scheme.
fields.mnemonic: ICDS covers: Pregnant women, Children under 6, Adolescent Girls (P-C-A-G). Remember 'P-C-A-G' like 'P-C-A-Ge' (Pregnant, Children, Adolescent Girls).

fields.question_text:
Which of the following correctly represent the three critical determinants of a healthy facility being declared as a First Referral Unit (FRU)?
1. Availability of emergency obstetric surgical interventions
2. Availability of immunization services
3. Blood storage facility
4. Newborn care

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: First Referral Units (FRUs) are healthcare facilities that provide comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care. The three critical determinants are: 1) Availability of emergency obstetric surgical interventions (e.g., C-sections), 3) Blood storage facility (for transfusions), and 4) Newborn care (e.g., sick newborn care units). Immunization services (2) are important but not a critical determinant for FRU status.
fields.concept_explanation: First Referral Units (FRUs) are part of India's public health system under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality. They serve as referral centers for primary health centers (PHCs) and community health centers (CHCs) by providing advanced care like emergency surgeries, blood transfusions, and specialized newborn care. Immunization is a preventive service typically provided at lower-level facilities like PHCs, not a defining feature of FRUs.
fields.mnemonic: FRU = F(First) R(Referral) U(Unit) → S(urgical care) B(Blood) N(Newborn). Remember: 'Surgical, Blood, Newborn' are the core services.

fields.question_text:
What is the correct increasing order of minimum age at which the following vaccines are administered to a child, as part of the National Immunization Schedule (NIS) after birth of child?
1. BCG vaccine
2. Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine
3. Rotavirus vaccine
4. Tetanus and adult diphtheria (Td) vaccine

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: The correct increasing order of minimum age for vaccine administration is: BCG (at birth) → Rotavirus (6 weeks) → Japanese Encephalitis (9 months) → Td (10 years).
fields.concept_explanation: The National Immunization Schedule (NIS) in India specifies the age at which vaccines are administered to children to ensure optimal immunity. BCG is given at birth or as early as possible. Rotavirus vaccine is administered starting at 6 weeks of age. Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine is given at 9 months, typically alongside the measles vaccine. Tetanus and adult diphtheria (Td) vaccine is administered at 10 years of age as a booster dose.
fields.mnemonic: B(irth) → R(otavirus) → J(apanese Encephalitis) → T(d). Remember as 'BRJT' or 'Baby Rides Joyfully To Ten'.

fields.question_text:
Under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme, ASHAs have been entrusted to carry out which of the following activities?
ASHAs are to search for suspected cases of leprosy in their villages and take them to the PHCs for diagnosis and treatment.

ASHAs arrange an amount of ₹5,000 as an incentive to each leprosy affected person in their village for undergoing reconstructive surgery.

ASHAs ensure that each leprosy affected person in their village receives micro-cellular rubber footwear for protection of insensitive feet.

ASHAs follow up all confirmed cases of leprosy in their village to ensure their treatment completion.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: ASHAs are responsible for searching suspected leprosy cases and taking them to PHCs (Activity 1) and following up confirmed cases to ensure treatment completion (Activity 4). Activities 2 and 3 are not part of ASHA's role under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme.
fields.concept_explanation: The National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at reducing the burden of leprosy in India. ASHAs (Accredited Social Health Activists) play a key role in early case detection, referral, and treatment adherence. They are not involved in providing financial incentives or distributing footwear, which are managed through other health system components.
fields.mnemonic: ASHAs ASK (Activity, Search, Keep) for leprosy: ASHA's role is to ASK (Activity 1) and ASK (Activity 4) for follow-up. Financial incentives and footwear are handled by other programs or departments.

fields.question_text: The cost of implementation of 'Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana' is borne by:
fields.option_c: Both Central Government and State Government
fields.option_d: Private institutions only as a part of their Corporate Social Responsibility
fields.explanation: The cost of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is shared between the Central and State Governments as per the specified funding pattern.
fields.concept_explanation: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2018 to provide health coverage to vulnerable populations. The funding is shared between the Central Government (60%) and State Governments (40%) for most states, except for North-Eastern and Himalayan states where the Central share is 90%. This collaborative funding model ensures equitable distribution of resources and shared responsibility in healthcare delivery.
fields.mnemonic: PM-JAY: Partners Make Jointly Assured Yojana (Central + State Governments share costs)

fields.question_text: All of the following are dashboard indicators used for monitoring of India Newborn Action Plan (INAP). Which one of them is an 'impact level indicator'?
fields.explanation: Neonatal mortality rate (NMR) is an impact-level indicator as it measures the actual outcome (deaths) in the target population, reflecting the success of interventions under INAP.
fields.concept_explanation: The India Newborn Action Plan (INAP) is a national strategy to reduce neonatal mortality to single digits by 2030. It uses a three-tiered monitoring framework: (1) Input indicators (resources, policies), (2) Process indicators (service delivery), and (3) Impact indicators (outcomes like mortality rates). Impact indicators directly measure the desired health outcome, such as neonatal mortality rate (NMR), which is the number of neonatal deaths per 1,000 live births. Other options like Caesarean section rate, exclusive breastfeeding rate, and percentage of preterm births are process or input indicators, not direct impact measures.
fields.mnemonic: I-N-M-R: Impact = Neonatal Mortality Rate. Remember 'I' for Impact and 'NMR' for Neonatal Mortality Rate.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following are health education models?
1. Medical model
2. Motivation model
3. Persuasion model
4. Social intervention model

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Health education models include Motivation model, Persuasion model, and Social intervention model. The Medical model is not a health education model but a framework for understanding health and illness.
fields.concept_explanation: Health education models are frameworks designed to influence behavior and promote health. The Motivation model focuses on internal drives to change behavior. The Persuasion model uses communication to convince individuals to adopt healthy practices. The Social intervention model involves community-level strategies to improve health outcomes. The Medical model, however, is a biomedical approach to diagnosing and treating diseases, not an educational framework.
fields.mnemonic: M-P-S: Motivation, Persuasion, Social intervention (Health Education Models). Medical model is separate (think 'M' for Medical, not part of Health Education).

fields.question_text: Who among the following has two general phases – first, simple pneumoconiosis and a second phase characterized by progressive massive fibrosis (PMF)?
fields.explanation: Anthracosis progresses from simple pneumoconiosis to progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) in its second phase.
fields.concept_explanation: Pneumoconiosis refers to lung diseases caused by inhalation of dust, leading to fibrosis. Anthracosis (coal worker's pneumoconiosis) has two stages: Stage I (simple pneumoconiosis with small nodules) and Stage II (progressive massive fibrosis with large fibrotic masses). Other options like Bagassosis (sugar cane dust), Byssinosis (cotton dust), and Siderosis (iron dust) do not follow this two-phase progression.
fields.mnemonic: A-N-T-H-R-A-C-O-S-I-S: 'A' for Anthracosis, 'N' for Nodules (simple phase), 'T' for Two phases, 'H' for Heavy coal dust, 'R' for Risk of PMF.

fields.question_text:
Consider the following statements about correlation between two variables:
The correlation is done between an independent variable X and a dependent variable Y.

The coefficient of correlation can range from –1 to ∞.

If coefficient of correlation (r) is equal to 1, it indicates there is no association between X and Y.

Correlation does not necessarily prove causation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
fields.explanation: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because correlation does not require a dependent/independent variable distinction. Statement 2 is incorrect as the correlation coefficient ranges from -1 to 1. Statement 3 is incorrect because r=1 indicates a perfect positive linear association.
fields.concept_explanation: Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables. The Pearson correlation coefficient (r) ranges from -1 to 1. A value of 1 indicates a perfect positive linear relationship, -1 a perfect negative linear relationship, and 0 no linear relationship. Correlation does not imply causation, as a third variable may influence both. The distinction between independent (X) and dependent (Y) variables is not required for correlation analysis, though it is essential for regression.
fields.mnemonic: CORrelation: C=Coefficient, O=Only -1 to 1, R=Range. Remember: 'Correlation is not Causation' (CINC).

fields.question_text:
With regard to lead poisoning, consider the following statements:
Coproporphyrin in urine is a useful screening test.

Hand washing before eating is an important measure of personal hygiene.

The use of d-penicillamine has been reported to be effective in management.

How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
fields.explanation: All three statements are correct regarding lead poisoning: Coproporphyrin in urine is a useful screening test, hand washing before eating is an important hygiene measure to prevent ingestion of lead-contaminated dust, and d-penicillamine is an effective chelating agent in management.
fields.concept_explanation: Lead poisoning occurs due to exposure to lead, which interferes with various body systems, particularly the nervous system. Coproporphyrin is elevated in urine due to disrupted heme synthesis. Hand hygiene prevents ingestion of lead-contaminated particles. d-penicillamine is a chelating agent used to reduce lead burden in the body.
fields.mnemonic: C-H-P: Coproporphyrin (Urine test), Hand washing (Hygiene), Penicillamine (Chelation therapy).

fields.question_text: A water body was inspected to look for the presence of mosquito eggs. It was observed that there were boat-shaped eggs, laid singly, not in clusters. The eggs also had lateral floats. Which one of the following diseases is most likely to be spread by the mosquito whose eggs were found?
fields.explanation: The described eggs (boat-shaped, singly laid, with lateral floats) are characteristic of Anopheles mosquitoes, which transmit malaria.
fields.concept_explanation: Mosquitoes of the genus Anopheles are primary vectors for Plasmodium parasites causing malaria. Their eggs are distinctively boat-shaped, laid singly, and have lateral floats for buoyancy. Other mosquitoes like Aedes (dengue/chikungunya) and Culex (Japanese encephalitis) have different egg-laying patterns and structures.
fields.mnemonic: Anopheles = 'A' for 'Alone' (singly laid eggs) and 'A' for 'Malaria' (disease).

fields.question_text:
In the National Health Policy 2017, a target of 90:90:90 has been set for HIV/AIDS. Which among the following are targets for which a 90% level has been set as part of 90:90:90 for HIV/AIDS?
Proportion of couples who have safe sex

Proportion of people living with HIV who know their HIV status

Proportion of adolescents who have access to contraceptives

Proportion of people receiving antiretroviral therapy who have viral suppression

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: The 90:90:90 target for HIV/AIDS in the National Health Policy 2017 refers to: 1) 90% of people living with HIV knowing their status, 2) 90% of those diagnosed receiving antiretroviral therapy, and 3) 90% of those on therapy achieving viral suppression. Only options 2 and 4 match these targets.
fields.concept_explanation: The 90:90:90 strategy was introduced by UNAIDS in 2014 as a global framework to end the HIV/AIDS epidemic by 2030. It aims to diagnose 90% of all HIV-positive people, provide antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 90% of those diagnosed, and achieve viral suppression in 90% of those treated. This ensures early detection, treatment access, and effective viral control to reduce transmission and improve health outcomes.
fields.mnemonic: Think '90-90-90 = Know-Treat-Suppress': 1) Know your status (90% know), 2) Treat with ART (90% treated), 3) Suppress virus (90% suppressed).

fields.question_text: The Sample Registration System (SRS), an important source of health information consists of continuous enumeration of births and deaths by an enumerator and an independent survey every six months by an investigator-supervisor. Which one of the following terms best describes this system?
fields.explanation: The SRS uses two independent recording systems (enumerator-based continuous enumeration and investigator-supervisor surveys) to cross-verify birth and death data, which is characteristic of a dual-record system.
fields.concept_explanation: A dual-record system involves two independent data collection methods to improve accuracy and reduce errors in vital statistics. The Sample Registration System (SRS) in India employs this method by having an enumerator record births and deaths continuously, while an investigator-supervisor conducts independent surveys every six months. The two datasets are then matched and reconciled to ensure completeness and accuracy.
fields.mnemonic: Think 'Dual = Two': Two independent records (enumerator + investigator) verify the same data (births/deaths).

fields.question_text:
Cross-over type of study designs are those in which each patient serves as his/her own control. In which of the following conditions is a cross-over study not suitable?
1. If the drug of interest cures the disease
2. If the drug is effective during all stages of the disease
3. If the disease changes radically during the period of time required for the study

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Cross-over studies are unsuitable when the drug cures the disease (as no second phase can be studied) or when the disease changes radically during the study period (as baseline conditions cannot be restored).
fields.concept_explanation: Cross-over study designs involve each participant receiving multiple treatments in a sequential manner, with their own baseline serving as control. This design is ideal for chronic, stable conditions where the disease state does not change significantly over time. However, it is inappropriate for conditions that are cured by the intervention (e.g., antibiotics for infections) or diseases that progress rapidly (e.g., acute myocardial infarction), as the carry-over effect or changing baseline invalidates the comparison.
fields.mnemonic: CROSS-OVER: Cures, Rapid changes, Or progressive diseases = Not suitable. Think 'CROSS' as 'Cannot Replicate Over Stable States'.

fields.question_text: In which one of the following diseases are the source of infection and reservoir of infection the same?
fields.explanation: In hookworm infection, the source of infection (contaminated soil with larvae) and the reservoir of infection (human host) are the same, as humans are the primary host and the environment serves as the source.
fields.concept_explanation: The source of infection refers to the immediate origin from which an infectious agent is transmitted to a host, while the reservoir of infection is the natural habitat where the pathogen normally lives, grows, and multiplies. In hookworm infection, the larvae (infective form) originate from contaminated soil (source), and humans (reservoir) are the definitive hosts where the parasite completes its life cycle. For other options: Cholera's reservoir is humans, but the source is contaminated water; Tetanus' reservoir is soil, but the source is contaminated wounds; Typhoid's reservoir is humans, but the source is contaminated food/water.
fields.mnemonic: Hookworm: 'Soil to Skin, Skin to Soil' — larvae from soil infect humans, and humans contaminate soil via feces.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Chikungunya fever?
1. It is usually transmitted by Culex mosquito.
2. A safe and effective vaccine is available for commercial use.
3. Incubation period is 4–7 days.
4. One of the prominent symptoms is arthropathy.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Statements 3 (incubation period 4–7 days) and 4 (prominent symptom arthropathy) are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect (Aedes mosquito transmits Chikungunya), and statement 2 is incorrect (no commercial vaccine available).
fields.concept_explanation: Chikungunya fever is an arboviral disease caused by the Chikungunya virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. The incubation period ranges from 2 to 12 days, with 4–7 days being a common duration. Key symptoms include high fever, rash, and severe arthralgia/arthritis (arthropathy), which can persist for weeks to months. Unlike some other arboviral diseases, no commercial vaccine is currently available for Chikungunya.
fields.mnemonic: CHIKUNGUNYA: C = Aedes mosquito (Culex is wrong), H = High fever, I = Incubation 4–7 days, K = Knee/ joint pain (arthropathy), U = Unvaccinated (no commercial vaccine).

fields.question_text: In which one of the following vector-borne diseases, the transmission chain is 'Man-Snail-Man'?
fields.explanation: The transmission chain 'Man-Snail-Man' is characteristic of Schistosomiasis, where humans are the definitive hosts, snails are intermediate hosts, and the disease is transmitted through contact with contaminated water.
fields.concept_explanation: Schistosomiasis, also known as bilharzia, is a parasitic disease caused by trematode flatworms of the genus Schistosoma. The life cycle involves humans as definitive hosts and freshwater snails as intermediate hosts. Eggs released by infected humans into freshwater hatch into miracidia, which infect snails. After development in the snail, infectious cercariae are released into water, which then penetrate human skin, completing the cycle. This 'Man-Snail-Man' transmission is unique to Schistosomiasis among the given options.
fields.mnemonic: Think 'S' for Snail and Schistosomiasis: 'S'nail 'S'chistosomiasis 'S'kin penetration.

fields.question_text:
Which of the following mosquito-borne diseases are transmitted chiefly by Aedes mosquito?
1. Dengue
2. West Nile fever
3. Yellow fever
4. Zika fever

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Dengue, Yellow fever, and Zika fever are primarily transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, while West Nile fever is chiefly transmitted by Culex mosquitoes.
fields.concept_explanation: Aedes mosquitoes are vectors for several arboviral diseases, including Dengue (DENV), Yellow fever virus (YFV), and Zika virus (ZIKV). These mosquitoes thrive in urban environments and breed in artificial containers. West Nile fever, caused by West Nile virus (WNV), is primarily transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, which prefer stagnant water bodies. Understanding the vector specificity is crucial for disease control and prevention strategies.
fields.mnemonic: Aedes = A for 'Africa' (Yellow fever), 'Asia' (Dengue), and 'Zika' (Zika fever). Remember: 'Aedes Ate Yellow, Asian, and Zika fruits.'

fields.question_text: Which one among the following is best defined as the interval of time between receipt of infection by a host and maximal infectivity of that host?
fields.explanation: Generation time is the interval between infection acquisition and maximal infectivity, distinguishing it from other periods like incubation or latent phases.
fields.concept_explanation: In infectious disease epidemiology, the generation time (or generation interval) refers to the duration from when a host acquires an infection to the point when they become most infectious to others. This is distinct from the incubation period (time from infection to symptom onset), latent period (time from infection to becoming infectious), and serial interval (time between successive cases in a chain of transmission). Generation time is critical for modeling disease spread and designing control measures.
fields.mnemonic: GENeration time = GENerates maximum infectiousness (GEN = GENeration, MAX = MAXimal infectivity)

fields.question_text:
Consider the following vaccines:
1. BCG Vaccine
2. Hepatitis B Vaccine
3. Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV)
4. Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)

What is the correct order of the above vaccines as per their sensitivity to heat (most sensitive to least sensitive) given in the National Immunization Schedule (NIS)?
fields.explanation: The correct order of sensitivity to heat (most to least sensitive) is OPV (4) > IPV (3) > Hepatitis B (2) > BCG (1).
fields.concept_explanation: Vaccines vary in their sensitivity to heat due to differences in their composition and stability. Live attenuated vaccines (like OPV) are generally more heat-sensitive than inactivated vaccines (like IPV and Hepatitis B) or live bacterial vaccines (like BCG). OPV is highly sensitive due to its live poliovirus component, while BCG, being a live bacterial vaccine, is more stable but still requires careful storage. Hepatitis B and IPV are inactivated vaccines with moderate heat sensitivity.
fields.mnemonic: OPIH-B: OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine) is Most sensitive, then IPV (Inactivated Polio Vaccine), then Hepatitis B, and BCG is Least sensitive.

fields.question_text:
Exposure to gases is a common hazard in industries. The gases can be classified as simple, asphyxiating and anaesthetic gases. Which among the following are asphyxiating gases?
1. Carbon monoxide
2. Chloroform
3. Cyanide gas
4. Hydrogen

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Asphyxiating gases are those that displace oxygen in the air or interfere with the body's ability to use oxygen, leading to suffocation. Carbon monoxide (1) and cyanide gas (3) are asphyxiating gases. Chloroform (2) is an anaesthetic gas, and hydrogen (4) is a simple asphyxiant but not classified as an asphyxiating gas in this context.
fields.concept_explanation: Asphyxiating gases can be categorized into simple asphyxiants (e.g., nitrogen, methane) that displace oxygen, and chemical asphyxiants (e.g., carbon monoxide, cyanide) that interfere with oxygen utilization at the cellular level. Carbon monoxide binds with hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin, reducing oxygen-carrying capacity. Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase in the electron transport chain, halting cellular respiration. Chloroform acts as an anaesthetic by depressing the central nervous system, while hydrogen, though a simple asphyxiant, is not typically classified under asphyxiating gases in industrial hazard contexts.
fields.mnemonic: Think 'CCC' for Asphyxiating Gases: Carbon monoxide, Cyanide, and Chemical asphyxiants. Chloroform is an anaesthetic (think 'C' for Chloroform and 'A' for Anaesthetic), and Hydrogen is a simple asphyxiant (think 'H' for Hydrogen and 'S' for Simple).

fields.question_text:
The Employees State Insurance Act, 1948 of India provides for certain benefits to employees. Which among the following are benefits to insured persons or to other dependents under the Act?
1. Disablement benefit
2. Funeral expenses
3. Maternity benefit
4. Travel benefit

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: The Employees State Insurance Act, 1948 provides for disablement benefit, funeral expenses, and maternity benefit to insured persons or their dependents. Travel benefit is not covered under the Act.
fields.concept_explanation: The Employees State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 is a social security legislation in India that provides medical and cash benefits to employees and their dependents in case of sickness, maternity, disablement, or death due to employment injury. The Act covers various benefits including disablement benefit (for temporary or permanent disablement), funeral expenses (up to a specified limit), and maternity benefit (for pregnant women). Travel benefit is not a provision under this Act.
fields.mnemonic: D-F-M: Disablement, Funeral, Maternity benefits are covered under ESI Act. Remember 'D-F-M' as 'Don't Forget Me' (benefits).

fields.question_text:
Which among the following vaccines best represent interventions that focus on cancer prevention too?
1. Hepatitis A vaccine
2. Hepatitis B vaccine
3. Hemophilus influenzae B vaccine
4. Human papilloma virus vaccine

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
fields.explanation: Hepatitis B vaccine prevents liver cancer (HCC) caused by chronic HBV infection, while HPV vaccine prevents cervical and other HPV-related cancers.
fields.concept_explanation: Certain vaccines provide cancer prevention by targeting oncogenic viruses. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and the HBV vaccine reduces HCC incidence. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is linked to cervical, oropharyngeal, and other anogenital cancers; the HPV vaccine prevents these infections and subsequent malignancies. Hepatitis A and Haemophilus influenzae B vaccines do not have cancer prevention roles.
fields.mnemonic: B for Both cancer prevention (HBV) and HPV vaccine prevent cancer. HAV and Hib don't have cancer links.

fields.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
     Statement-I: While calculating the number of expected pregnancies per year in an area, a correction factor (usually 10%) is added to the expected number of live births in the year in the area.

     Statement-II: All the pregnancies in the area may not be registered by the health worker in the area.

     Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
fields.option_a: Statement-I and Statement-II are independently correct, and Statement-II is a correct explanation for Statement-I.
fields.option_b: Statement-I and Statement-II are independently correct, but Statement-II is not a correct explanation for Statement-I.
fields.option_c: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
fields.option_d: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
fields.explanation: Statement-I is correct as a 10% correction factor is often added to live births to estimate pregnancies (accounting for stillbirths/abortions). Statement-II is correct as not all pregnancies are registered due to underreporting or missed cases. However, Statement-II does not explain Statement-I, as the correction factor is applied for statistical completeness, not solely due to underreporting.
fields.concept_explanation: In preventive and social medicine, fertility rates are often calculated using live births as a proxy. However, pregnancies include live births, stillbirths, and abortions. A correction factor (e.g., 10%) is added to live births to estimate total pregnancies, accounting for unreported cases. Underreporting (Statement-II) is a reason for using correction factors but does not directly explain why the correction is applied to live births to estimate pregnancies.
fields.mnemonic: Live births + Stillbirths + Abortions = Total Pregnancies. Correction factor accounts for missing data, not just underreporting.

fields.question_text: Thickened ventricular wall with normal diastolic function is a feature of
fields.explanation: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is characterized by thickened ventricular walls with normal diastolic function, often presenting with asymmetric septal hypertrophy and outflow tract obstruction.
fields.concept_explanation: Cardiomyopathies are diseases of the heart muscle, with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy being the most common cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes. It is often inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and can lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, and sudden death. The key feature is the thickening of the ventricular wall, particularly the septum, which can lead to outflow tract obstruction and impaired diastolic function. However, in the early stages, diastolic function may be preserved, making it a key distinguishing feature.
fields.mnemonic: HOCM: Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy, think 'thick' ventricular walls

fields.question_text:
In which of the following cases does paradoxical splitting occur?
Severe aortic stenosis

Right bundle branch block

Right ventricular pacing

Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
fields.explanation: Paradoxical splitting of S2 occurs when the second heart sound (S2) splits during expiration and merges during inspiration, typically due to delayed closure of the aortic valve. This is seen in conditions causing delayed left ventricular ejection (e.g., LBBB, right ventricular pacing, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy) or early right ventricular ejection (e.g., RBBB). Severe aortic stenosis does not cause paradoxical splitting; it typically causes a single S2 or widened splitting.
fields.concept_explanation: Splitting of the second heart sound (S2) occurs due to asynchronous closure of the aortic (A2) and pulmonary (P2) valves. Normally, inspiration delays P2 (due to increased venous return to the right heart), causing physiological splitting. Paradoxical splitting occurs when A2 is delayed (e.g., in conditions like LBBB, RV pacing, or HOCM), causing splitting during expiration and merging during inspiration. Conditions like RBBB cause widened splitting due to delayed P2. Severe aortic stenosis typically causes a single S2 or reversed splitting (A2 before P2) due to prolonged LV ejection time.
fields.mnemonic: P-R-A-D: Paradoxical splitting occurs in Pulmonary delay (RBBB), Right ventricular pacing, Aortic delay (LBBB, HOCM), and Delayed LV ejection (severe AS may not cause it). Remember: 'P-R-A-D' for causes of paradoxical splitting.

fields.question_text: A patient with peripheral edema has the following findings on clinical examination: A soft systolic murmur at the lower left sternal border with raised JVP showing prominent C-V wave. The murmur increases in intensity on deep inspiration. The most likely valvular abnormality is
fields.explanation: The murmur described is a holosystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border, increasing with inspiration (Carvallo's sign), with a prominent C-V wave in the JVP, indicating tricuspid regurgitation.
fields.concept_explanation: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a valvular heart disease where the tricuspid valve fails to close properly during systole, causing blood to flow backward from the right ventricle into the right atrium. This leads to increased right atrial pressure, manifesting as a prominent C-V wave in the jugular venous pulse (JVP). The murmur is typically holosystolic, best heard at the lower left sternal border, and increases with inspiration due to increased venous return to the right heart (Carvallo's sign). Other options like VSD or mitral regurgitation have different murmur characteristics and locations.
fields.mnemonic: TRiPS: Tricuspid Regurgitation increases with Inspiration, Prominent C-V wave, Systolic murmur at lower left sternal border.

fields.question_text: Kussmaul's sign is a clinical feature of
fields.explanation: Kussmaul's sign (paradoxical rise in JVP during inspiration) is classically seen in constrictive pericarditis due to impaired right ventricular filling.
fields.concept_explanation: Kussmaul's sign occurs when jugular venous pressure (JVP) rises paradoxically during inspiration. In constrictive pericarditis, the rigid pericardium prevents normal cardiac expansion during diastole, leading to increased venous return pressure during inspiration. This is distinct from normal physiology where JVP falls with inspiration (negative intrathoracic pressure). Other conditions like restrictive cardiomyopathy may also show this sign, but constrictive pericarditis is the classic association.
fields.mnemonic: Kussmaul's = Constrictive pericarditis (K-CP). Remember: 'Kussmaul's sign is a sign of a stiff pericardium (constrictive pericarditis) that can't expand!'

fields.question_text: A patient has a cardiac murmur that is best heard at the right second intercostal space. It increases with expiration. Also, the murmur reduces in intensity during sustained handgrip but increases in intensity on inhalation of amyl nitrite. The likely lesion is
